chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Bird's reception in Kansas City versus the Savoy audience
summary: He says Kansas City listeners liked Bird without needing to understand him, while at the Savoy the crowd ignored Bird's Body and Soul but cheered Jimmy Forrest.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, did Bird have that -- the big impact on the band like he did have the impact on everybody later at that time, did (inaudible)?
Well, Bird not only had impact on the band, when we were around Kansas City with the small group and when Bird wasn't playing with me, he had impact on Kansas City.
Kansas City -- I always said that they didn't know what all he was doing, but you take anybody that was around Kansas City in them days and they always loved to

Because they understood while -- how would you say it? I don't mean they understood it musically for the -- you know what I mean. But they understood that they like it. They liked it. See, when we went to New York, we'd be in New York, just blowing. Bird would get up and blow "Body and Soul" -- we had a heck of an arrangement on "Body and Soul" -- and he'd blow that "Body and Soul" and ain't nothing else to blow. But Jimmy Forrest come back around and when Bird get through blowing, they never even clapped their hands. But when Forrest get through, the house would break up. And it used to make me so mad. Here's what I mean. I said, "Well, what are these people thinking about?" But that wouldn't have happened in Kansas City.
You mean they didn't hear it.
This was at the Savoy in New York, yes.
Well, yeah. Now that's very interesting because what Bird was blowing -- I mean the Savoy was mostly geared to dancing, wasn't it?
Now then, would you say that what Bird played was sort of good to dance to?
